The **Imjin War** (also known as the **Japanese invasions of Korea** or the **Japanese Invasions of 1592–1598**) was a series of military conflicts between the Japanese forces, led by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and the Korean Joseon dynasty, with assistance from Ming China. Here’s a quick overview: | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Timeframe** | 1592–1598 | | **Key Players** | • **Japan** – Toyotomi Hideyoshi’s forces (≈300,000 troops)
• **Korea (Joseon)** – King Seonjo’s army (≈200,000 troops)
• **Ming China** – Imperial forces (≈400,000 troops) | | **Causes** | • Hideyoshi’s ambition to conquer China via Korea.
• Korean refusal to allow Japanese troops to use its territory as a staging ground. | | **Major Phases** | 1. **First Invasion (1592–1593)** – Japanese forces captured Seoul and much of the peninsula; Korean navy, led by Admiral Yi Sun-sin, inflicted heavy losses on Japanese supply lines.
2. **Second Invasion (1597–1598)** – Renewed Japanese attacks; Korean and Ming forces eventually pushed back, culminating in the Battle of Noryang (1598). | | **Key Battles** | • Battle of Hansan Island (1592) – Yi Sun-sin’s naval victory.
• Battle of Myeongnyang (1597) – Yi Sun-sin’s 13‑ship fleet defeated a larger Japanese fleet.
• Battle of Noryang (1598) – Final major naval engagement. | | **Outcome** | • Japan was forced to withdraw; the war ended with the Treaty of 1598, leaving Korea devastated but intact.
• The war highlighted the importance of naval power and the vulnerability of land‑based supply lines. | | **Legacy** | • Strengthened Korean naval tradition.
